review.summary:
This review covers WP08 only. I worked from the supplied review summaries, dispositions and evidence; I did not inspect the source files. The prior findings marked BLOCKER or MAJOR have documented closures:
- **Undefined `html` in the panel test:** the excerpt was incomplete, and the follow-up review closed it.
- **Stale popup/step target:** repaired, and the follow-up found no blocker; the 52 browser states now pass on the current revision.
- **Typecheck:** the reviewer couldn't check it, but it now passes.
- **settings/features truncated excerpt:** a byte-for-byte check shows only the title changed (功能模組管理 → 功能模組).
- **Hard-coded step-type picker labels:** fixed. The supplied excerpt now reads every label from `funnelStepLabels`, the groups use Chinese names, and the `value` keys are unchanged.

The navigation review confirms that the app-shell changes keep the same hrefs and the same role/feature flags. The editor and reports reviews confirm that stored IDs, enum keys and calculations are unchanged.

The retained MINOR/NIT items are acceptable and don't block delivery: optional names when an external caller passes ids without names, the existing 一頁式網站 sidebar term, Unicode shaping, and raw cents, which predate WP08.

Some gaps remain:
1. None of the supplied review summaries can be traced to `landing-page-puck-config.tsx` or `funnel-block-library.ts`. Those files may hold Puck component/block type keys that saved page documents depend on, so the "persisted identifiers unchanged" requirement depends on files no reviewer is shown to have read.
2. None of the summaries cover the dashboard files (`dashboard/*`, `team-performance-dashboard.tsx`) or several funnel UI files, even though dashboard vocabulary is a core WP08 requirement.
3. The 52 browser/a11y states are focused on the funnel editor. The stated coverage doesn't include the app-shell navigation (including the changed aria-label) or the dashboard loading states.

The canonical gate is NOT_RUN. The browser runs use synthetic adapters, not an authenticated full-app end-to-end run. This review does not certify test or release success, and it does not certify the full set of 20 work packages.

findings.area: Puck component config keys / block library type identifiers (whole files)
findings.issue: None of the supplied review summaries can be traced to these two files. Their keys are likely written into saved page documents, so the requirement that persisted identifiers stay unchanged hasn't been checked here.
findings.evidence: The lineage covers: batch1 (display-only, files not listed), the panel test follow-up, funnel-display-labels, app-shell/navigation pages, FunnelElementInspector, the report excerpts, and the editor integration (funnel-step-pages-editor / workspace-editor). No summary or disposition names landing-page-puck-config.tsx or funnel-block-library.ts. The 'no stored-key mutation' statements are each limited to the code their reviewer was given.
findings.impact: Puck stores component `type` keys in documents. If WP08 translated a config key or block id instead of only its label, existing saved landing pages would fail to render or would lose blocks. Synthetic-adapter browser tests built from new fixtures wouldn't detect that.
findings.recommended_fix: Run a scoped read-only review of the WP08 diff for both files. Confirm that only `label` and description strings changed, and that component keys, block ids, field names and default prop keys are byte-identical to the base revision.
findings.required_test: A regression test that loads a fixture saved before WP08 (using the original component type keys) through the current Puck config and the block library, and checks that every block resolves and renders. Also add a test asserting that the set of config/block keys equals the base set.

findings.area: Dashboard visible vocabulary and loading-state copy
findings.issue: WP08's core requirement includes dashboard vocabulary, but none of the supplied review summaries cover the dashboard copy, the loading components or team-performance-dashboard.tsx. Several funnel UI files are also not traceable to any review: funnel-goal-picker, funnel-list, funnel-template-gallery-picker, funnel-webinar-experience, funnel-webinar-settings and funnel-popup-preview.
findings.evidence: The lineage summaries cover navigation, funnel labels, the inspector, reports and the editor integration. The dashboard files appear in the source scope, and dashboard test files exist (presumably among the 79 targeted tests), but no reviewer finding or disposition mentions them.
findings.impact: Mixed English/Chinese wording or inconsistent wording could remain on the dashboard, the merchant's main page, and only unit tests would have checked it. That's lower risk than the identifier issue because these files appear to be display-only.
findings.recommended_fix: Run a short scoped copy review of the dashboard files and the funnel UI files listed above, checking against the terminology snapshot. Or state explicitly that batch1 covered them.
findings.required_test: Confirm that the dashboard loading/KPI tests assert the final Chinese labels, and that the terminology snapshot includes the dashboard and team-performance terms.

findings.area: Navigation aria-label and nav a11y browser coverage
findings.issue: The 52 browser/a11y states are described as covering funnel-editor actions, deleted targets, same-node reset, reports and settings dialogs. They don't explicitly include the app-shell navigation (including the corrected aria-label) or the dashboard loading states, so the a11y requirement for those surfaces rests on unit snapshots only.
findings.evidence: The evidence statement lists 52 states: chromium/firefox desktop/mobile actions, deleted targets, same-node reset, reports and settings/dialogs. The navigation review noted that one aria-label changed in app-shell and had a spacing defect, which was later fixed.
findings.impact: An accessible-name regression in the sidebar or mobile navigation could ship without detection, because synthetic-adapter runs that don't render the shell would miss it.
findings.recommended_fix: Add one or two app-shell a11y states (desktop sidebar and mobile nav), or document that existing states render the shell and assert its landmarks and names.
findings.required_test: An axe/a11y browser check of the app shell on desktop and mobile that asserts the navigation landmark's accessible name and the localized link names.
